title: Damiano Marchiafava passes his doctoral defense
body: Danny defended successfully. Hooding follows, but the defense was the event. His dissertation covers calcium handling in dystrophic muscle, including the finding that the plasma membrane calcium pump PMCA1 is downregulated before cytosolic calcium dysregulation appears.
alt: Danny at the lectern after his defense seminar, beside his closing slide

title: Third R15 awarded by NIAMS
body: The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases funded a third successive R15 for the genetic repair of muscular degeneration in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with Xiaotian Dai as co-investigator. The lab has held continuous external funding since 2015.

title: Mars analog paper accepted at Scientific Reports
body: Aalimah Akinosho, with undergraduates Nora Armstrong and Zachary Benefield, reports behavioral deficits in animals raised for six generations under Mars analog gravity and hypomagnetic fields.

title: Muscle architecture remodels during locomotion
body: Adina Fazyl and high school researcher Anbu Anbu, contributing equally, show activity dependent remodeling of muscle architecture during distinct locomotor behaviors. Published in Biology Open.

title: Independent validation of transgenerational pathogen avoidance
body: Aalimah Akinosho and Jordan Alexander independently validated the transgenerational inheritance of learned pathogen avoidance, published in eLife. Information about a threat outliving the animal that met it is one of the three kinds of disruption the lab studies.

title: Invited seminar at Wayne State University
body: Andres gave the Department of Biological Sciences seminar in Detroit, titled Tracing the Origins of Dysfunction in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Multiscale Approach to Early Pathophysiology. The talk argued that the resting calcium set point is already displaced before dystrophic muscle has begun to contract, which makes the earliest pathology a problem of regulation rather than of injury. Hosted by Eleni Gourgou, with a day of meetings that included Joseph Roche, who works on Duchenne muscular dystrophy in the Physical Therapy Program there.
alt: Andres with Joseph Roche at Wayne State University, the Detroit skyline behind them

title: Mackenzie Jones in the Image of Research exhibition
body: Mackenzie's entry, Coloring the Secret Life of Muscles, shows calcium reporters firing along the body wall muscle of freely moving animals. The lab builds its own reporters and its own analysis, and this is what that work looks like before it becomes a figure.
alt: Mackenzie Jones beside her Image of Research entry, nine worms imaged with calcium reporters on a black field

title: Rene Wilderman presents at the University Research Symposium
body: Rene asked whether the corticosteroids given to Duchenne patients help smooth muscle the way they help striated muscle, measuring egg laying rate as the readout. The preliminary answer is that they do not, and that vamorolone, despite its reputation for reduced side effects, did not restore egg laying either. With Mackenzie Jones as second author.
